clue.text: It's a happy knack to sink into a calm state perchance

indicators.note: the word for sinking is placed into the middle of the calm state

parts.note: serenity is a state of calm
to dip is to sink briefly

explanation.surface: Advice on luck: drift into a tranquil frame of mind and good fortune may follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container. 'perchance' points to the chance discoveries the word describes, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipity is the faculty of making fortunate discoveries by accident, a lucky gift.

clue.text: Good time for press work?

parts.note: read as the hour an ... newspaper goes to press, or a pleasant time to do the ironing

explanation.definitionFit: Late afternoon going into night is when evening papers are printed and when chores are often done.

clue.text: See 2
Dismal around Holyhead, but tender

indicators.note: the word for dismal goes around the single letter taken from the head of Holy

parts.note: dingy means drab and gloomy
read as Holy's head, its first letter H

explanation.surface: A gloomy description of the Welsh port of Holyhead that still finds it gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: Holyhead is a Welsh ferry port, but here it is split as 'Holy head', giving H. 'tender' is a noun: a small boat serving a larger one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a small boat ferrying people to a ship, and a dinghy is just such a craft.

clue.text: Fairy-like being took off and died

parts.note: a peri is a fairy or sprite in Persian myth
shed means removed, as clothing

explanation.surface: A sprite flew away and came to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To have perished is to have lost one's life.

clue.text: Granted a favour for being patient, maybe

definitions.meaning: given a special pleasure, as when a friend pays for dinner
a hospital patient receives medical care from a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone rewarded for waiting calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: given an indulgence, or given medical care as a patient.

clue.text: Protection at hand in a cul-de sac?

definitions.text: Protection at hand in a cul-de sac?

parts.words: Protection at hand in a cul-de sac?
parts.note: read as guarding at close range, or as the safety of a dead-end street, which in Britain may be called a close

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a close is a residential cul-de-sac.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodyguards near at hand give near protection; a dead-end road's safety fits the second reading.

clue.text: Dispel banshees; their day is over

indicators.note: to dispel is to scatter, so the letters of banshees are scattered and regrouped

explanation.surface: An exorcist's order to drive off wailing spirits whose time has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Has-beens are people whose period of fame or usefulness has ended.

clue.text: Wherein events one dreamt can be realised, notice

indicators.note: realised in the sense of made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A promise that the things you have dreamt of may come true here, as an advert would say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be realised' rearranges EVENTS, I and DREAMT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice in a paper announcing a sale or service is a public promotion of that kind.

clue.text: Left a British composer in N. Ireland

definitions.note: a place found in Northern Ireland, a port town

parts.note: Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A British composer departed for Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the town's location: Larne is a port in County Antrim.
explanation.definitionFit: Larne is a ferry port on the County Antrim coast of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: One whose charges are invariably small

definitions.text: One whose charges are invariably small

parts.words: One whose charges are invariably small
parts.note: charges read as children in someone's care rather than fees

explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after young children always has little ones in her care.

clue.text: Windows on the stars?

parts.note: windows set in a roof, looking up at the night sky, while the sky's lights are the stars themselves

explanation.definitionFit: Roof windows face upwards, giving a view of the heavens.

clue.text: Schedule used to spread the fare

definitions.meaning: a timetable or list arranged in rows and columns
the piece of furniture on which a meal is laid out

explanation.surface: A timetable for serving a buffet.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable is a set of rows and columns; dinner is laid out on the furniture of the same name.

clue.text: Slip along to despatch, it's said

indicators.note: signals that the word for despatch is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to despatch is to kill, to slay

explanation.surface: An instruction to hurry along and send something off, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' takes SLAY by sound. The definition describes the sledge gliding over snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge pulled over snow is a vehicle that glides along.

clue.text: Set a time approximately

indicators.note: approximately suggests the letters are only roughly as given, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fix a rough time for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'approximately' rearranges SET A TIME, and the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a rough guess at a figure or time is to judge it approximately.

clue.text: Principal relaxation fitment to the car

parts.note: the head is the principal of a school
rest is relaxation

explanation.surface: The chief comfort accessory fitted to a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushioned support on top of a car seat for the back of the skull.

clue.text: Complaint that sounds like a moan over Greek territory

indicators.note: tells the solver the words are heard aloud

parts.note: a moan is a sigh, placed over Attica, the region of Greece around Athens

explanation.surface: An ailment that is a groan about a part of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds like' takes SIGH on top of ATTICA by ear, giving the spelling SCIATICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sciatica is a painful ailment of the nerve running down the leg.

clue.text: Downpour making it hard to see

definitions.meaning: a torrential fall of rain or water
a clouding of the eye's lens that impairs vision

explanation.surface: Heavy rain that ruins visibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent of water and an eye condition clouding the lens share the name.

clue.text: Notable work our dean composed

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A remarkable piece written by the cathedral dean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges OUR DEAN. 'Notable' means having musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a musical or poetic form with a recurring refrain, a work set to notes.

clue.text: Reports of an explosive nature

parts.note: reports read as bangs rather than accounts, or as angry outbursts

explanation.definitionFit: Explosions make loud bangs, and angry rebukes are outbursts too.

clue.text: Devastating winger with a family name

parts.note: a locust is a winged insect that devastates crops

explanation.surface: A destructive flyer with a surname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family name' means a name in biological classification, not a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusta is a genus of locusts, a name used in taxonomy.

clue.text: Made fun of one in shabby attire

explanation.surface: A scruffy dresser who was mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To have teased someone, and to be dressed in tatters, share the word.

clue.text: Upright type as Brutus was

definitions.meaning: printing type with vertical, unslanted letters
Brutus, assassin of Julius Caesar, was a citizen of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: An honest person, like Brutus.
explanation.definitionFit: Typeface that is not slanted, and a citizen of ancient Rome, share the name.

clue.text: Facetious centre of an ideology without order

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for the noun: the state of having no government

indicators.note: the word for facetious becomes the centre of the other pieces

parts.note: an ism is a doctrine or ideology
arch means playfully teasing

explanation.surface: A joking core to a belief system with no order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' signals the container. The definition is a phrase for the state the doctrine seeks, a society without rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the political belief in a society with no government or rulers.

clue.text: French current Eire's adopted

indicators.note: adopted means taken up and changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s counts here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: France's money taken up by the Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted' rearranges EIRES. 'currency' is a misprint for 'current', meaning a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isère is a river flowing through south-eastern France into the Rhône.

clue.text: Confining within certain limits

parts.note: restricting an animal to the reach of a rope tied to a post

explanation.definitionFit: Tying a goat to a stake on a rope restricts its range.

clue.text: Woolly lot of wild geese

definitions.meaning: a flock of geese in flight

explanation.surface: Wool and a flight of wild geese.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose coil of yarn and a flight of geese share a collective name.

clue.text: Entertainment all good sports enjoy

parts.note: good sports read as easygoing people, who like playful frolics

explanation.definitionFit: Lively frolics and amusement are enjoyed by people who take things in good spirit.
